content: Certainly. Cefotetan is an antibiotic classified under the cephalosporin group. It is used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections and is also administered prophylactically before and during certain surgical procedures to prevent infections. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and does not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use Cefotetan Carefully read and follow all preparation and usage instructions provided by the manufacturer. When mixing the medication with the appropriate IV fluids, ensure proper technique. Consult your pharmacist for detailed guidance. Before administration, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use if abnormalities are present. If using a frozen pre-mixed solution, thaw the container at room temperature or in the refrigerator. If thawed in the refrigerator, allow it to sit at room temperature for at least one hour before use. Do not thaw using a water bath or microwave. After thawing, shake the container well and check for leaks by squeezing it. Discard the solution if the container leaks. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. To help maintain a consistent schedule, use the medication at the same time(s) each day. Complete the full prescribed treatment course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may result in a relapse of the infection. Learn proper storage and disposal methods for needles and medical supplies to ensure safety. Side Effects Common side effects include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, it may cause loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, cefotetan may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Symptoms include persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, and blood or mucus in the stool. Contact your doctor immediately if these symptoms occur. Prolonged or repeated use of cefotetan may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but may include rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Seek immediate medical attention if these occur. Precautions Inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to cefotetan, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other medications. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages while taking this medication and for at least three days after completing the course. Alcohol may interact with cefotetan, causing adverse effects such as flushing, nausea, vomiting, and headache. Cefotetan may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccines. This medication passes into breast milk in small amounts. While no significant effects on milk production or the breastfed infant have been reported, discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of cefotetan or increase the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Cefotetan may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., urine glucose tests, serum or urine creatinine tests), potentially causing false results. Inform laboratory personnel that you are using this medication. Overdose In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S. or 1-844-764-7669 in Canada). Missed Dose If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage Different brands or packaging of cefotetan may have specific storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging or consult your pharmacist for instructions. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Important Notes This summary does not include all possible information about cefotetan. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. Cefotetan is generally considered safe during pregnancy, with no evidence of fetal risk in controlled studies. However, discuss its use with your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Additional Information Cefotetan is a second-generation cephalosporin that provides broad coverage against gram-negative and anaerobic bacteria, with some activity against gram-positive bacteria. It is primarily excreted unchanged in the urine, with a small percentage eliminated via feces. Prolonged use of cefotetan may lead to overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Monitor patients closely for signs of superinfection, and take appropriate measures if it occurs.
